title: Business Office Standard — Billing Holds on the Patient Financial Account
content:
A Patient Financial Account is placed on billing hold when a review that could change what the patient owes is opened. While on hold the account receives no statements, late fees, final notice or placement.

## Reviews that place a hold

| Hold reason | Review |
|---|---|
| balance dispute | the patient disputes a charge |
| insurance review | a claim the patient says was billed to the wrong payer, or one awaiting a coordination-of-benefits questionnaire |
| hardship review | a financial-hardship review |
| estate review | a review after the patient's death |

## Conditions

1. **Matching case.** A hold for any reason requires an open billing case of the matching type: the patient has an open billing case of the type that matches the hold reason. This is read from the patient's billing cases, not from the patient's statement.
2. **Dispute window.** A balance dispute is accepted only for a charge first statemented recently. The dispute is raised no later than the tier's dispute window counted from the date of the first statement issued after the disputed charge was posted. The window is counted in calendar days starting the day after that statement date, and a dispute raised on the last day still qualifies.

**Hypothetical window.** A charge is posted on day 0; the first statement after it is dated day 10; the dispute window is 60 days. Day 11 is the first counted day and day 70 the last. A dispute raised on day 70 qualifies; one raised on day 71 does not.

## Release

- A hold is released when the case behind it is decided.
- A balance-dispute hold is released no later than the tier's dispute hold maximum, in days, after the date the hold started, even if the case is still open.
- An estate-review hold runs the tier's estate-review hold period.
- A coordination-of-benefits hold that is not answered within the tier's coordination-of-benefits response time leaves the pended charge as patient responsibility on release.
